_note: This document is COMPLETE for its owner class: every field Credit Risk Policy
may set is stated, and none is inherited from a code default. `resolve_params`
is called with complete=True and names any field that fell back.
It is also BOUNDED: there is no field in this file that Credit Risk Policy may
not change, and no field they may change is missing from it. The statutory
fields do not appear -- not because they were omitted, but because
`--owner=credit_risk_policy` cannot emit them and `resolve_params(..., as_owner=
'credit_risk_policy')` rejects a document that contains one:
params document from origin 'git:config/affordability/policy.json@a41f9c2'
sets 'deductions.paye_table_override', which is owner_class=statutory
(owned by credit_systems, transcribing the gazette). This owner may not
set it. 1 field rejected; nothing was applied.
That rejection is spec 6.2's 'unreachable, not a convention'.
Table CONTENTS are values and live in tables/policy/ as dated files, not
inline here -- a 1 152-cell internal norms table in a params document is
unreviewable and undiffable. What lives here is the POINTER TO A VERSION,
and only for tables this owner owns. Changing it is a value change: free,
no recompile, a bundle swap.
Note the asymmetry. Credit Risk Policy may pin which version of their own
tables is live. They may not pin a statutory one: those resolve from
decision_date and from nothing else, because pinning a statutory table is
how a 2026 assessment quietly starts using 2027 norms.
